claims.text: A machine-learning model trained on existing melting-property data can predict melting temperatures of refractory materials.
The machine-learning model can predict thermodynamic melting properties beyond melting temperature.
Machine learning can predict melting properties more efficiently than traditional DFT methods.
A training dataset containing melting properties for multiple refractory materials is required.
Machine-learning algorithms can generalize melting-property relationships from known materials to new refractory materials.
The model learns relationships between material composition and melting properties.
The model learns relationships between material structure and melting properties.
Learning composition–structure–property relationships enables rapid melting-property predictions.
Machine-learning predictions can be made without performing expensive DFT calculations for each new material.
The model will predict melting temperatures for new refractory materials with reasonable accuracy.
The model will predict entropy of fusion for new refractory materials with reasonable accuracy.
The model will predict enthalpy of fusion for new refractory materials with reasonable accuracy.
The model will predict volume change at the melting point for new refractory materials with reasonable accuracy.
Current DFT-based melting-property calculations are computationally expensive.
Current DFT-based melting-property calculations are time-consuming.
Prediction accuracy depends on the quality of the training data.
Prediction accuracy depends on the quantity of training data.
Prediction accuracy depends on the complexity of the refractory materials.
